title: Rationalise the Numerator
text:
Multiply by the conjugate:

$$\frac{\sqrt{x+h} - \sqrt{x}}{h} \times \frac{\sqrt{x+h} + \sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x+h} + \sqrt{x}}$$

The numerator becomes:

$(\sqrt{x+h})^2 - (\sqrt{x})^2 = (x+h) - x = h$

title: Take the Limit
text:
Now take the limit as $h \to 0$:

$$f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{1}{\sqrt{x+h} + \sqrt{x}}$$

As $h \to 0$, $\sqrt{x+h} \to \sqrt{x}$:

$$f'(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{x}} = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}$$

Using power notation: $f'(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^{-\frac{1}{2}}$
